map_scale_facts:
NOTE ON COVERAGE: Only 13 city pairs are listed, not the 25 requested. The shared web-search budget for this run ran out partway through ('limit: 200 WebSearch calls per turn'), so no more searches could be made. No pairs were invented. A follow-up run can collect more (London-Manchester, Warszawa-Berlin, Roma-Milano, Lisboa-Madrid and so on).
MAP SCALE: The mainland ETS2 map is about 1:19 (racinggames.gg article 'Euro Truck Simulator 2 Is Roughly 1:19'; trucksimulator.wiki.gg user blog 'Map Scale in ETS2 and ATS'; ATS is 1:20 for comparison). The UK is about 1:15, inherited from UK Truck Simulator, while Germany and Austria came from German Truck Simulator at 1:19. Cities are compressed much less: commonly quoted as 1:3, but a ProMods forum post says major cities are about 1:5 and small ones about 1:10, so this is medium confidence. SCS announced 'Project UK Rework' (reported 19 Oct 2025) with no stated new UK scale. A UK scale of 1:20 appears only in a fan suggestion on the SCS forum, so the UK scale in the Nov 2026 build is uncertain if the rework has shipped.
DISPLAYED KM: The km shown in game (job market, route advisor, odometer, WoT logs) are not raw world-space metres. Outside cities they are scaled up by the scale factor (about x19), so they roughly match real-world road distances. Evidence: the ets2-telemetry-server Telemetry.md describes a 'scale' factor (example value 19) applied to distance and time to compensate for the map scale. The 'Real time and distance' mods exist to show the unscaled distance instead. Sample values match too: Calais-Duisburg 436 km in game vs about 370-400 km in reality; Hamburg-Berlin 339 km vs about 290 km. The exact factor applied inside city zones and in the UK (15 vs 19) is not confirmed by a primary source.
FERRIES: Community sources (Steam ETS2 discussions from 2014-2015, including the 2,200 km achievement thread) say ferry and train (Eurotunnel) legs ARE included in a job's total distance shown in the offer and completion screen, but do NOT count as 'driven' km because the truck is static. In one example, the total was above 2,200 km including the ferry and 2,069 km driven without it. A route-planner tool notes that the game does not show ferry or train leg distances separately. A ProMods forum thread notes that the GPS may prefer ferries, which cuts road km and thus income. These sources are old, so verify in the current build: medium confidence. Separately, a forum post (Jan 2026) says the WoT external job market currently caps jobs at about 5,000 km.
time_scale_facts: Default ETS2 time compression on the open road (mainland) is about 1:19. One in-game hour is 60/19, about 3.16 real minutes (the Truck Simulator Wiki 'Time Compression' page and Steam threads round this to about 3 real minutes; one Steam comment says 1:20). Inside cities, depots and some rest areas, time runs at about 1:3, so one in-game hour is about 20 real minutes (Steam forum; SCS forum thread on Krakow time flow scale). For the UK, the time scale is commonly quoted as 1:15 to match the UK map scale, which gives one in-game hour of about 4 real minutes. That figure is low-to-medium confidence: the sources found tie 1:15 to the UK map scale but none explicitly confirms the UK time scale, and the UK rework may change it. Ferry and train crossings skip ahead: the game fast-forwards the in-game clock by the crossing duration while only a loading screen passes in real time. Conversion formula: real_minutes = ingame_hours x 60 / k, with k = 19 for the mainland open road, about 15 for the UK (uncertain) and 3 in cities. Because displayed km are scaled by the same factor as time, driving at a displayed 80 km/h covers a displayed 80 km per in-game hour. So, as a rough rule, the real time for a mainland job is displayed_km / avg_speed_kmh x 60 / 19 minutes, plus extra for city segments at 1:3. Player reports of 3-5 real minutes per in-game hour on the road reflect slowdowns from traffic and cities.
